components.gap: Gnedenko-Kolmogorov Section 35 (pp. 171-172) defines attraction of a law F to an arbitrary limit law V (suitable constants A_n, B_n), the domain of attraction of V, and states that two laws of the same type have the same domain of attraction so that one may speak of the domain of attraction of a type; Theorem 1 is stated for "a (proper) normal law". The routed definition (def:p15-nda-law-and-moments, normal-domains-of-attraction.tex 16-52) defines attraction only to chi and contains neither the general definition nor the type-invariance claim (the route has only the one-direction reduction N(m,tau^2) -> chi inside the examples proof, annex 812-820). Supply the definition and the type claim with its proof.

components.gap: The historical chain is not on the route: Durrett (p. 152) attributes Theorem 3.4.14 to Levy and calls it "the last word" on convergence to the normal law; the 1954 footnote to Section 35, Theorem 1 (p. 172) attributes the theorem to A. Ya. Khintchine, W. Feller and P. Levy; and Section 35 (p. 172) asserts, by appeal to Section 33, that exactly the stable laws have non-empty domains of attraction, calls the determination of these domains a fundamental problem whose complete solution the section gives, and contrasts the very wide normal domain with the domains of the other stable laws, which contain only laws whose character recalls the attracting law. The routed boundary (def:p15-nda-historical-boundary, 301-312) mentions only Sections 19-26 as separate presentations. Supply these attributions and claims, reported with attribution where not proved.
